## What changed

Bug fixes for the `require-mode` gate added in `fork.6` and `fork.7`. If you
ran `lat init` on an existing project, upgrade — several of these could leave
your `lat.md/` in a bad state.

- **Fixed: `lat init` could silently switch off checks you had already turned
  on.** When it added `require-mode` to your root index, it sometimes added a
  second frontmatter block instead of editing the one already there. The old
  block stayed in the file and looked fine, but nothing read it any more. Any
  `require-code-mention` or `mode` setting in it stopped working, and
  `lat check` still passed.

- **Fixed: answering "yes" could leave your project half set up.** On some
  frontmatter, `lat init` created the four mode directories and rewrote your
  root index, then said it could not set the flag — and never offered again.
  You were left with a restructured tree, the gate off, and no way to finish.
  It now works out whether it can set the flag *before* it asks, and does
  nothing at all if it cannot.

- **Fixed: `lat init` refused frontmatter it could actually handle.** These all
  work now: `lat: {tags: [x]}` on one line, `lat: &anchor`, an empty `lat:` next
  to another key with a list under it, and unusual indentation. Comments in your
  frontmatter are kept.

- **Fixed: `require-mode: yes` looked like it worked and did nothing.** YAML
  reads `yes` as text, not as true, so nothing was enforced — and `lat init`
  stopped offering to help because it thought the flag was set. Only `true` and
  `false` are accepted now, and anything else is reported by `lat check mode`.
  `require-mode: false` is a permanent "no thanks" and is never asked about
  again.

- **Fixed: the "N documents would need a mode" count was wrong.** It counted
  files by where they sat rather than by what they said, and included files that
  were already broken. It now shows only what turning the gate on would newly
  cost.

- **Fixed: if you said no, `lat init` could commit that answer to your repo.**
  The "declined" marker is written to `lat.md/.cache/`, which is only ignored by
  git in projects that `lat init` created. Committed, it would have stopped
  `lat init` offering to everyone else on your team. It now ignores itself.

- **Fixed: `lat init` could crash partway through** with a raw error if
  `lat.md/.cache/` was not writable. It now reports the problem and carries on.

- **Fixed: only one mode directory was linked from the root index** if your
  index already mentioned one of them, which left three directories that
  nothing pointed at and broke `lat check index`.

- **Fixed: releases built by hand had no changelog or diff link.** A shallow
  fetch in the release workflow cut off the history the notes are generated
  from. Such a release could also tag the wrong commit.

## Upgrading

```
npm i -g --prefix ~/.local/lat https://github.com/PlebeianTech/lat.md/releases/latest/download/lat.md-latest.tgz
```

Then in your project:

```
lat init
lat check
```
